links.outcome: AI performance reported by site and scanner across multiple sites and vendors
links.effect: AI performed well per-site (AUC ≥ 0.83) at the patient-level independent of scanner age and field strength; six machines from two manufacturers across six sites.
links.quote: AI performed well per-site (AUC ≥ 0.83) at the patient-level independent of scanner age and field strength.

links.outcome: AI compared with MDT-supported radiologists on same data for GG≥2 prostate cancer detection
links.effect: Per patient, Pi was non-inferior to radiologists (10% margin), AUC 0.91 vs 0.95; sensitivity 95% vs 99%, specificity 67% vs 73%.
links.quote: Evaluated per patient, Pi was non-inferior to radiologists (considering a 10% performance difference as acceptable), with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.91 vs. 0.95.

links.outcome: Performance on separate validation dataset from different hospitals than training
links.effect: Validation on separate dataset (252 patients, six sites) from different UK hospitals gave AUC 0.91 for the AI, non-inferior to radiologists.
links.quote: We compared a new AI solution, validated on a separate dataset from different UK hospitals, to the original multidisciplinary team (MDT)-supported radiologist's interpretations.

screen.reason: Retrospective multi-centre external validation of a commercial deep learning tool (Pi) for prostate cancer detection on MRI compared against radiologist interpretations, without testing a specific deployment practice or workflow safeguard.
